title: The Goodwife of Cairo and Her Four Gallants (简体中文)

keywords: the goodwife of cairo and her four gallants
full_text:
In Cairo lived a virtuous and beautiful woman named Sitt al-Husn, whose husband, a noble merchant, was unjustly detained abroad on a commercial dispute.
During his absence, four influential men of the city—the Chief Kazi, the Grand Vizier's secretary, the Captain of the Watch, and a wealthy grain merchant—shamelessly pestered her with unwanted advances, each abusing his authority to demand her favor.

Sitt al-Husn, determined to protect her honor and punish their insolence, devised a masterstroke of comedic justice.

She sent secret, identical invitations to each of the four suitors, inviting each to visit her house that evening at staggered intervals of half an hour.
She then hired an expert carpenter to build a massive cedar wardrobe with four separate, deep interior compartments, each fitted with a spring bolt that locked from the outside.

At dusk, the Chief Kazi arrived in his velvet judicial robes, eager and boasting. Before he could speak three words, Sitt al-Husn cried: 'Heavens! My husband's fierce brother has returned! Quick, hide in this cabinet!'
The Kazi scrambled into the first compartment, and she snapped the lock shut!

Half an hour later, the Grand Vizier's secretary arrived, perfume wafting from his silk sleeves. A sudden knock sounded at the door. 'Woe is me!' she cried. 'The watchmen have surrounded the house! Conceal thyself in this wardrobe!' The secretary leaped into the second compartment, which locked behind him!

Next arrived the Captain of the Watch, who in turn was terrified by a pretended alarm and shoved into the third compartment!
Finally, the wealthy grain merchant arrived, only to be pushed into the fourth compartment!

With all four pompous suitors securely locked in separate compartments, Sitt al-Husn sent a messenger to the Governor of Cairo:
'Your Excellency, I have in my possession a rare antique wardrobe containing four extraordinary curiosities of the city, which I wish to present to the municipal council.'

The Governor and his retinue assembled in her courtyard.
With a radiant smile, Sitt al-Husn turned the keys:
Out tumbled the Chief Kazi in rumpled robes, the Secretary covered in cedar dust, the Captain of the Watch trembling with humiliation, and the Grain Merchant clutching his knees!

The Governor stared in shock, then burst into roaring laughter along with the entire assembly.
Sitt al-Husn addressed the court:
'Behold, your Excellency! These are the guardians of law, security, and commerce in Cairo, who use their titles to harass an unprotected wife while her husband travels!'

The Governor, admiring her brilliant wit and courage, dismissed the corrupt officials, appointed honorable replacements, and sent an armed escort to bring her husband safely home with royal indemnity.
The tale became celebrated as Cairo's greatest victory of female intellect over arrogant folly.
moral: Virtuous wit and ingenious resourcefulness protect honor while teaching foolish suitors an unforgettable lesson. [ZH]
